title: Quickstart & Architecture
summary: Bootstrap a high-performance documentation handbook in less than 3 minutes. Zero build configuration required.
content:
DocuCraft is an opinionated, static-first documentation engine engineered for developer happiness, sub-50ms cold loads, and 100% Lighthouse audit scores. Built with zero runtime dependencies.
ℹ️
Production Ready: DocuCraft produces pure semantic HTML5, modern CSS, and lightweight ES6. It deploys out-of-the-box to GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify, or Vercel with zero server costs.

Architecture Overview

Traditional documentation tools often bundle megabytes of client-side JavaScript, hydration overhead, and bloated Webpack runtimes. DocuCraft flips this paradigm:

  • Static AST Generation: Markdown and MDX are compiled ahead-of-time into optimized semantic DOM nodes.
  • Zero Hydration Tax: Navigation, table of contents, and search run entirely in pure vanilla ES6 (less than 12KB gzip).
  • Client-Side Full Text Indexing: In-memory prefix trie algorithm delivers instant search results without Algolia credentials.
  • Accessible by Default: WCAG 2.1 AA compliant, screen-reader friendly code blocks, keyboard navigable (Tab, Ctrl+K).

System Prerequisites

Before installing the CLI, ensure your environment meets the minimum version constraints:

Runtime / Tool Supported Versions Recommended
Node.js >= 18.16.0 LTS Node.js 20.x or 22.x LTS
pnpm / npm pnpm >= 8.0, npm >= 9.0 pnpm for instant caching
Git >= 2.34.0 Git 2.40+ with commit signing

Step 1: Install DocuCraft CLI

Install the global CLI utility using your preferred package orchestrator:

# Global installation via pnpm
pnpm add -g @docucraft/cli

# Verify version
docucraft --version
# Output: docucraft/2.4.0 darwin-arm64 node-v20.11.0
# Global installation via npm
npm install -g @docucraft/cli

# Verify version
docucraft --version
# Global installation via yarn
yarn global add @docucraft/cli

# Verify version
docucraft --version
# Direct standalone binary installation for Linux / macOS
curl -fsSL https://get.docucraft.dev/install.sh | bash

Step 2: Scaffold Your Handbook

Run the interactive initializer to generate a standard documentation repository with TypeScript configuration and sample guides:

docucraft init my-developer-portal --template standard

# Navigate into project directory
cd my-developer-portal
💡
Interactive Prompts: The initializer will ask for your Project Title, Base URL (e.g. https://docs.mycompany.com), GitHub Repository URL, and primary theme accent color.

Step 3: Start Local Hot-Reload Server

Launch the built-in development web server with instant Markdown hot-module reloading:

docucraft dev --port 4000 --open

Your documentation handbook is now live at http://localhost:4000. Edits to any Markdown file in ./docs reflect in under 40 milliseconds.

Standard Directory Tree

A typical DocuCraft handbook adheres to this clean filesystem hierarchy:

my-developer-portal/
├── docs/                      # Markdown and MDX content sources
│   ├── 01-getting-started/
│   │   ├── index.md           # /docs/getting-started/
│   │   └── quickstart.md      # /docs/getting-started/quickstart
│   ├── 02-api-reference/
│   │   ├── authentication.md  # /docs/api-reference/authentication
│   │   └── endpoints.md       # /docs/api-reference/endpoints
│   └── 03-deployment/
│       └── github-pages.md    # /docs/deployment/github-pages
├── assets/                    # Static images, diagrams, custom SVGs
│   └── architecture-diagram.svg
├── docucraft.config.ts        # Primary configuration manifest
├── package.json               # Scripts & dependencies
└── tsconfig.json              # Optional TypeScript typings

title: Installation & Environments
summary: Detailed installation instructions for local development, CI/CD pipelines, containerized environments, and air-gapped setups.
content:
DocuCraft is distributed as both an npm package, a standalone compiled binary for macOS/Linux/Windows, and a minimal Docker container (under 24MB).

Package Manager Options

You can add DocuCraft as a local dev-dependency directly into your project root so all team members use the exact pinned version:

# Add as pinned project development dependency
pnpm add -D @docucraft/cli@^2.4.0

# Add build scripts to package.json
npm pkg set scripts.docs:dev="docucraft dev"
npm pkg set scripts.docs:build="docucraft build"
npm pkg set scripts.docs:serve="docucraft serve --dist ./dist"

Docker Containerized Setup

For organizations requiring strict container sandboxing or air-gapped CI workers, pull the official Alpine-based container:

# Pull the lightweight Alpine image
docker pull ghcr.io/docucraft/docucraft:2.4.0-alpine

# Run local documentation server mounting your ./docs folder
docker run --rm -it \
  -p 4000:4000 \
  -v $(pwd)/docs:/app/docs \
  -v $(pwd)/docucraft.config.ts:/app/docucraft.config.ts \
  ghcr.io/docucraft/docucraft:2.4.0-alpine dev

CI/CD Automated Verification

Validate broken links, invalid code blocks, and missing image references automatically inside your GitHub Actions pipeline:

# .github/workflows/docs-validation.yml
name: Documentation Lint & Build

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'docucraft.config.ts'

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with:
          version: 9
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint Markdown & Dead Links
        run: pnpm docucraft check --strict

      - name: Compile Static Distribution
        run: pnpm docucraft build

Air-Gapped & Offline Bundles

If operating inside high-security networks with zero external WAN connectivity, download the standalone archive containing all bundled font assets, search indexing routines, and icon sets without remote CDN calls:

# Download offline bundle archive
curl -O https://releases.docucraft.dev/v2.4.0/docucraft-offline-v2.4.0.tar.gz

# Extract and run
tar -xzf docucraft-offline-v2.4.0.tar.gz
./docucraft/bin/docucraft serve --offline

title: Configuration Reference
summary: Exhaustive reference for docucraft.config.ts. Learn how to configure custom themes, navigation trees, analytics, and plugins.
content:
DocuCraft utilizes a strongly typed TypeScript or JSON configuration file located at your repository root. Full IDE auto-completion is provided via JSDoc and TypeScript definitions.

Configuration Overview

The configuration file orchestrates your handbook's global metadata, navbar items, sidebar hierarchies, search algorithms, and custom code theme palettes.

Annotated docucraft.config.ts

Here is an enterprise-grade configuration exhibiting all core capabilities:

import { defineConfig } from '@docucraft/types';

export default defineConfig({
  // Global Project Identity
  title: 'DocuCraft Developer Handbook',
  tagline: 'High-velocity technical documentation engine for software teams',
  baseUrl: 'https://docs.docucraft.dev',
  favicon: '/assets/favicon.svg',

  // Version Control & SCM
  scm: {
    provider: 'github',
    repo: 'mujtabacloud/docucraft-documentation-theme',
    branch: 'main',
    docsDir: 'docs',
    showEditLink: true,
    editLinkText: 'Suggest an edit on GitHub'
  },

  // Navigation Bar Top Links
  navbar: {
    logo: {
      text: 'DocuCraft',
      version: 'v2.4.0',
      badge: 'STABLE'
    },
    items: [
      { text: 'Handbook', link: '/docs/quickstart', activeMatch: '^/docs/' },
      { text: 'API Specs', link: '/docs/api-reference' },
      { text: 'Changelog', link: 'https://github.com/mujtabacloud/docucraft/releases' },
      {
        text: 'Versions',
        items: [
          { text: 'v2.4.0 (Latest)', link: '/docs/quickstart' },
          { text: 'v2.3.1 (Maintenance)', link: '/v2.3/' },
          { text: 'v1.9.0 (LTS)', link: '/v1.9/' }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },

  // Design Tokens & Code Highlight Theme
  themeConfig: {
    accentColor: '#38bdf8', // Electric Cyan
    fontFamilySans: '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif',
    fontFamilyMono: '"SF Mono", "Fira Code", monospace',
    defaultTheme: 'dark', // 'dark' | 'light' | 'system'
    codeHighlight: {
      theme: 'github-dark-dimmed',
      showLineNumbers: true,
      copyButton: true
    }
  },

  // Search Engine Configuration
  search: {
    provider: 'local', // 'local' (In-memory trie) | 'algolia'
    maxResults: 8,
    keyboardShortcut: 'ctrl+k'
  }
});

Design Tokens & Brand Colors

DocuCraft allows CSS variable overrides directly via your custom stylesheet custom.css without having to rebuild dependencies:

/* custom.css */
:root {
  --doc-accent: #0284c7;             /* Primary Brand Color */
  --doc-accent-glow: rgba(2, 132, 199, 0.25);
  --doc-bg-main: #090d16;            /* Deep navy dark mode */
  --doc-code-bg: #040711;            /* Terminal editor contrast */
  --doc-border: rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.14);
}

Markdown Plugins (KaTeX, Mermaid)

Render mathematical formulas with KaTeX or architectural sequence diagrams with Mermaid simply by enabling them in markdownPlugins:

⚠️
SSR Pre-rendering: All Mermaid diagrams and KaTeX LaTeX formulas are pre-compiled during docucraft build. Zero heavy browser parsing scripts are downloaded by your users.

title: Authentication & API Keys
summary: Authenticate requests using Bearer tokens, workspace API keys, and cryptographically verified HMAC signatures.
content:
Every request to the DocuCraft Cloud API must be authenticated over HTTPS. Unauthenticated requests return a standard 401 Unauthorized JSON payload.

Bearer Token Authorization

Include your personal access token or service account key in the HTTP Authorization header prefixed with Bearer:

curl -X GET "https://api.docucraft.dev/v1/workspaces" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer dc_live_98a7f1e6b0294e1d" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
import { DocuCraftClient } from '@docucraft/sdk';

const client = new DocuCraftClient({
  apiKey: process.env.DOCUCRAFT_API_KEY! // 'dc_live_...'
});

const workspaces = await client.workspaces.list();
console.log(workspaces);
import os
import requests

api_key = os.environ.get("DOCUCRAFT_API_KEY")

response = requests.get(
    "https://api.docucraft.dev/v1/workspaces",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"}
)

print(response.json())
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "https://api.docucraft.dev/v1/workspaces", nil)
	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("DOCUCRAFT_API_KEY"))
	
	client := &http.Client{}
	resp, _ := client.Do(req)
	fmt.Println("Status:", resp.Status)
}

Generating Scoped API Keys

DocuCraft supports granular Principle-of-Least-Privilege (PoLP) scopes. You can generate keys restricted solely to read operations or build triggers:

Scope Identifier Permitted Actions Risk Level
docs:read Query public and private handbook schemas Low
docs:write Push markdown commits and deploy revisions Medium
admin:all Workspace member management and billing access High

HMAC-SHA256 Signature Header

For webhook consumers and enterprise SSO callbacks, all event payloads are signed using your workspace webhook secret key via HMAC-SHA256:

// Verify inbound webhook signature in Node.js
import crypto from 'node:crypto';

export function verifyWebhookSignature(payload: string, signature: string, secret: string): boolean {
  const hmac = crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret);
  const digest = 'sha256=' + hmac.update(payload).digest('hex');
  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(digest), Buffer.from(signature));
}

Rate Limit Specifications

API requests are throttled per API key according to your workspace tier:

  • Open Source Tier: 1,200 requests / minute
  • Enterprise Tier: 25,000 requests / minute

When throttled, the API returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with standard RFC 6585 headers:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1730678400
Retry-After: 42

title: REST API: Deployments
summary: Trigger automated documentation builds, check deployment status, and inspect build latency via the REST API.
content:
The Deployments API empowers CI/CD bots and Git webhook triggers to compile and publish new revisions of your documentation handbook without accessing the command line.

POST /v1/deployments

Submits a build manifest to the distributed edge compilation queue.

POST https://api.docucraft.dev/v1/deployments

Request Body Parameters

Field Type Required Description
environment string (enum) Required Target distribution environment: "production" or "preview".
commit_sha string Required Full 40-character or 7-character Git commit hash being built.
branch string Optional Git branch name. Defaults to "main".
auto_rollback boolean Optional If true, reverts to previous release if health checks fail. Defaults to true.

Live Interactive API Tester

Test the deployment orchestrator directly from this handbook. Click Send Request to execute a simulated request to the edge runner:

POST
Request Payload (JSON):
Response: Ready (Click Send) 
{
  "hint": "Click 'Send Request' to execute simulated deployment."
}

Response Schema Specification

A successful deployment registration returns HTTP 201 Created with the following JSON model:

{
  "id": "dep_9b4c10e82f71",
  "object": "deployment",
  "status": "queued",
  "environment": "production",
  "commit_sha": "71ef3b6",
  "branch": "main",
  "urls": {
    "live": "https://handbook.company.com",
    "inspect": "https://app.docucraft.dev/deployments/dep_9b4c10e82f71"
  },
  "created_at": "2026-11-03T18:24:00Z"
}

title: Troubleshooting & Error Index
summary: Resolutions for common compiler errors, broken hyperlinks, image rendering anomalies, and custom domain SSL issues.
content:
Encountering build warnings or hydration failures? Consult this systematic diagnostic guide engineered by the DocuCraft core maintainers.

Standard Error Code Index

Error Code Underlying Root Cause Recommended Remediation
ERR_LINK_BROKEN Relative Markdown hyperlink targets a missing .md file Run docucraft check --fix-links to auto-correct path
ERR_CONFIG_INVALID Syntax error or schema violation in docucraft.config.ts Validate schema with docucraft config validate
ERR_AST_PARSE_FAIL Unclosed HTML tag or malformed JSX inside Markdown Check the line and column number reported in terminal output
ERR_AUTH_EXPIRED API key or Bearer token has exceeded its TTL lifecycle Generate a renewed API key in your workspace console

Resolving Broken Internal Links

When reorganizing chapters or renaming files, references can become stale. The DocuCraft link verifier scans all anchors before building:

# Run link auditor in report mode
docucraft check --links

# Automatically create redirects for renamed files
docucraft check --links --generate-redirects

Large Monorepo Node Out-Of-Memory

If compiling documentation handbooks exceeding 5,000 pages within a massive monorepo, allocate additional heap memory to the Node.js V8 runtime:

# Set max old space size to 4GB
NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=4096" docucraft build

Custom Domain SSL & DNS CNAME

When deploying to custom apex domains (e.g. docs.yourcompany.com) via GitHub Pages or Cloudflare, ensure your DNS provider points to the edge CDN:

Record Type Host / Name Target Value TTL
CNAME docs mujtabacloud.github.io. Automatic (300s)
💡
Still blocked? Open an issue on our official GitHub Issues tracker or connect with community engineers on Discord.
